messages.subject: Apache proxying
parts:
Hi,

I'm testing Apache proxying against your Shiny service as you've suggested. It only works if I replace 'SockJS("/sockjs/szakacs/test2",null,{debug:true})' with 'SockJS("http://glimmer.rstudio.com/sockjs/szakacs/test2",null,{debug:true})' in the generated source code. I have the following config in my server:

ProxyPass /shiny/ http://glimmer.rstudio.com/szakacs/test2/
ProxyPassReverse /shiny/ http://glimmer.rstudio.com/szakacs/test2/
RedirectMatch permanent ^/shiny$ /shiny/

I'm not an Apache guru, I've copied it from the RStudio instructions. Any suggestions how this config can be modified? Or can your generated code be changed to work with this config?

Thanks, Laszlo

messages.subject: Re: Apache proxying
parts:
Apologies for dropping in late on this, but from what I understand about sockjs is that it will use the most efficient transport based on the browser. Thus, websockets are chosen for modern browsers and apache won't ever be able to proxy those requests.

I'm speculating here, but one possible solution could have RStudio's Shiny server detect that a client is requesting an app through a proxy (by inspecting certain HTTP headers?) and have the sockjs engine downgrade the transport to the lowest common denominator.

Just a quick and dirty demonstration that it could work behind Apache: http://us.planimeter.hu/shinyApacheTest2
I've put the following (with full sockjs url) into index.html after the body tag:

<script>
Shiny.createSocket = function() {return new SockJS("http://glimmer.rstudio.com/sockjs/szakacs/test2",null,{debug:true});};
</script>

messages.subject: Re: Apache proxying
parts: If you don't mind a non-port-80 port, you could just serve it up directly from runApp, no proxy required. As long as the R process doesn't crash or hang you should be fine. Just make sure to start it using "screen" or "nohup" so it doesn't exit when you close your ssh session.

messages.author: 9e1d805a26f6d719
messages.subject: Re: Apache proxying
parts:
Ah, that seems to work. FWIW, this is the steps I used:
  • Spin up a basic 64-bit Amazon Linux AMI. Log in via ssh.
  • Do "yum install R R-devel" to get R and the ability to build packages.
  • Start R. Install the shiny package via the instructions in the beta email. Also install other packages needed.
  • In the AWS console, set up a security group that allows connections to 8100 from your.ip.address/31. I had to fiddle with this a few times until it seemed to take.
  • From R, library(shiny); runExample("01_hello") should work
  • Install your server.R and ui.R (and if needed other files).
  • R -e "shiny::runApp('.')"
With a free micro instance, it all works, but those VMs are not fast. Easily 4 or 5 times slower than my MacBook Air.

 -Harlan

messages.subject: Re: Apache proxying
parts:
Sarabjeet,

Try running like this:

runExample("01_hello", launch.browser=FALSE)

I suspect the problem is that runExample tries to open up a web browser by default, which is not going to work remotely on an AMI machine. Note that runApp doesn't do this, so you won't need that option for your own code.

I doubt you're having a permissions issue, given what you've described...
